extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent attorneys, IP professionals, defendants, and in-house counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Creating graphical or tabular claim charts that break patent claims into limitations and map evidence (products, prior art, specifications) to those limitations for purposes such as infringement, invalidity, prosecution, or licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete breakdown of each claim into elements/limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The main purpose of Patent claim chart is to show the complete breakdown of each constituent into its elements or limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing a claim and breaking it down into several limiting components is the first step in creating a claim chart. The claim chart presents all the data analyzed in a patent claim and is used to prove or analyze usage of the claimed invention in products, services, or standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate interpretation of each claim element (not just keywords)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to understand the interpretation of each element rather than just limiting to synonyms or keywords comprehensively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid superficial keyword/synonym matching. Determine the correct legal and technical scope of each limitation and use that interpretation when mapping evidence or prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence mapping for infringement (Evidence of Use / EOU) — satisfy the 'all elements test/rule'
rubrics_metrics.description: An Evidence of Use (EOU) or Infringement Claim Chart shows how a product or technique is accused of infringement, including each claim element to fulfill the 'all elements test/rule' for infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For infringement charts, demonstrate with specific evidence how each and every claim limitation is present in the accused product/service/standard. Use the chart to support Initial or preliminary infringement contentions (PICs), licensing presentations, or expert reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity charting to show anticipation or obviousness (Chart of References)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Invalidity Chart, also known as a 'Chart of References', depicts the patent’s invalidity owing to anticipation or obviousness and is typically prepared by a defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map prior art references to claim limitations to show anticipation (exact limitation present) or obviousness (combination of references or reasoning). Use these charts in invalidity analysis during litigation, reexamination, or PTAB proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction/interpretation charts tying claim language to specification and literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Plaintiffs and defendants construct a Claim Construction or Claim Interpretation Chart, which shows patent specifications or technical literature citations with accurate claim language interpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cited portions of the specification and relevant technical literature to support the proposed meaning of claim terms. These charts assist in claim construction disputes and ensure claimed terms are grounded in the intrinsic/extrinsic record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose chart type and tailoring for the proceeding or purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim charts can be created for several purposes, such as the PTO’s reexamination during the prosecution stage or Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB’s) validity assessment of a patent. Examples include PICs, domestic industry (DI) charts used in ITC importation actions, expert claim charts, licensing charts, and design patent charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate chart format and level of detail based on the forum (litigation, ITC, PTAB, prosecution), procedural posture (preliminary contentions vs. expert report), and audience (judge, arbitrator, opposing counsel, licensee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use claim charts to analyze novelty and prior art relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purpose of invalidity analysis in litigation, Claim charts assist in confirming or refuting the novelty of a claim in relation to the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly show where prior art anticipates each limitation or how combinations render claims obvious. Use clear citations and side-by-side mappings to support novelty conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use claim charts to verify presence of every limitation for infringement analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: During infringement investigation and litigation, Claim charts aid in confirming or disputing whether each and every limitation of the claim is included in a good, service, or standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document factual evidence (e.g., product specs, screenshots, standards text, reverse-engineering results) that corresponds to each limitation. Be explicit about gaps or elements not found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format choice: graphical or tabular representation as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent claim chart can be a graphical or tabular (for use as evidence of use) representation of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tabular layouts for clear side-by-side mapping of claim language to evidence/references; graphical depictions can aid visual understanding for presentations or expert exhibits. Ensure the chosen format is admissible and fits the target audience's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customization, subject-matter expertise, and delivery expectations for quality charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Customized Reports: Based on the requirements of the customer and the target area, we provide solutions and modifications. A pool of excellent subject matter experts provides effective and efficient detailed reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality claim charts should be tailored to the client's objectives, prepared or reviewed by SMEs for technical accuracy, delivered with appropriate speed and cost considerations, and formatted to meet procedural or licensing needs.
